clue.text: Despondency I spread about

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of I and spread are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits to spreading gloom wherever they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the seven letters of I SPREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Despondency is low spirits, the loss of all hope.

clue.text: Spotted divine fruit inside

indicators.note: inside means the fruit goes within the letters for divine

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine's degree
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone saw holy fruit within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'saw', but means marked with spots; 'inside' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Dappled describes something marked with patches of a different colour, as a horse's coat.

clue.text: Increases — one's distance from the ground?

explanation.surface: Raising how far one stands above the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is 'step's up': one stair's height above the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up is to raise or intensify; a stair is a short way up off the floor.

clue.text: Excuse for party in capital

indicators.note: in places the party inside the word for capital

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate or capital
LIB is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: A reason to skip a celebration in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but means excellent: A1, written with the letter I for the figure one; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse.

clue.text: The odd messenger may be craftily dodging duty

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
a runner carries messages

explanation.surface: A strange courier might be a cunning tax dodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The odd messenger' reads as an oddball; 'duty' is customs duty, so this is a smuggler of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person smuggled alcohol to avoid customs tax.

clue.text: Started again to add up in a rush

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the word for a rush

parts.note: a rush is a reed, the waterside plant
to add up is to sum

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly restarts their sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a rush' reads as haste, but a rush is the plant, a REED, which holds SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to take something up again after a pause.

clue.text: Plunder Winchester, for example

explanation.surface: Looting the cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester suggests the English cathedral city, but it is the firearm maker.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to ransack; a Winchester is a well-known make of long gun.

clue.text: Get rid of smooth metal perhaps

parts.note: to scrap is to discard
to iron is to smooth out creases

explanation.surface: Throw away and flatten some metal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is waste ferrous material collected for recycling.

clue.text: Music master

parts.note: a plain description of a distinguished conductor or musician

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title is given to an eminent conductor or composer.

clue.text: Leaves a just reward

explanation.surface: Someone walks out and gets what they deserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the idiom 'just deserts', pronounced like dessert-less 'deserves'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserts means abandons; deserts are also what one deserves.

clue.text: Reward that may be paid as a matter of policy

definitions.text: that may be paid as a matter of policy

explanation.surface: A bonus handed out as company policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition puns on policy: an insurance policy is paid for in regular instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: A premium is a bonus or prize, and also the regular sum paid for insurance cover.

clue.text: Footnote to army group: it is needed in operations

indicators.note: to here means added on to, so the footnote goes after the army group

parts.note: a force is a body of troops
PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: A footnote appended to a military unit's report explains what is needed in operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operations' suggests military ones after the army group, but these are surgical.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons use the pincer-like instrument to grip tissue during surgery.

clue.text: With us details can produce weariness

indicators.note: can produce signals that the letters of us details are worked into something new

explanation.surface: Going through the fine print with us is exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can produce' rearranges the nine letters of US DETAILS; 'With' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental tiredness and lack of energy.

clue.text: Father's half-hearted sales-talk

definitions.note: here Father's is read as Father is

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the two letters at the heart of the word is lost

parts.note: patter is glib sales-talk

explanation.surface: Dad's sales pitch lacks conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: PATTER has a double T at its centre; dropping half of that heart leaves the answer. The 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is the Latin word for a parent, used in old-fashioned British slang for one's dad.

clue.text: Appropriate share of bath at home

parts.note: a dip is a quick bath or swim
in means at home

explanation.surface: Taking your fair share of the bathwater at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip in is to help oneself to a portion of something shared.

clue.text: He provides regular press hand-outs

parts.note: suggests a spin doctor issuing press releases, but describes a shopkeeper selling daily papers

explanation.surface: A press officer issues routine statements.
explanation.definitionFit: This shopkeeper sells daily papers and magazines over the counter.

clue.text: No good at all for use in a riot

indicators.note: riot signals that the letters of for use in a run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is useless as a weapon in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a riot' looks like the setting, but 'in a' is fodder and 'riot' alone signals rearranging FOR USE IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means wicked or criminal, wholly bad.

clue.text: Wild record band on quickest route to success

parts.note: fast can mean wild, as in fast living
a track is one band of a vinyl record

explanation.surface: A wild album by a group heads straight for the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record band' suggests a recording group; here it is one band on a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a route to promotion faster than the usual one.

clue.text: Forceful argument makes solving this difficult

explanation.surface: An angry exchange makes the crossword tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard words are angry or harsh remarks in a quarrel; tricky vocabulary also makes a puzzle hard.

clue.text: Energetic fellow who hurtles around?

indicators.note: around signals the letters of hurtles are shifted about

explanation.surface: A lively man rushing about everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges HURTLES; 'who' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-getter who works aggressively is called this.

clue.text: No answer

parts.note: reads as silence, but describes an answer that is the word no

explanation.definitionFit: A declining of a request, saying no, is a rejection.

clue.text: A troubled reign in west Africa

definitions.note: names a place found in west Africa rather than being a synonym for it

indicators.note: troubled signals that the letters of reign are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A turbulent rule somewhere in western Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges REIGN; 'A' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a landlocked country, and a major river, of west Africa.

clue.text: It should have a safety pin in it

definitions.text: It should have a safety pin in it

parts.words: It should have a safety pin in it
parts.note: suggests a nappy or garment, but means the pin keeping a bomb from going off

explanation.surface: A baby's nappy needs a pin through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand bomb has a safety pin that stops it exploding until pulled.

clue.text: Tries to stop son entering repeated exams

indicators.note: entering means son goes inside the repeated exams

parts.note: resits are exams taken again

explanation.surface: A parent tries to stop their boy taking exams again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts S inside RESITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or fight against something.

clue.text: A capital seat I snuggle into

indicators.note: snuggle into means I nestles inside the seat

parts.note: a sofa is a seat

explanation.surface: Someone curls up on a couch in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snuggle into' puts I inside SOFA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Lacking a game to play — or rivals

definitions.text: Lacking a game to play — or rivals

parts.words: Lacking a game to play — or rivals
parts.note: read literally, the word means without a contest; in its usual sense it means having no equal

explanation.surface: A team with no fixture, or no one to compete against.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means unrivalled, peerless, beyond compare.

clue.text: Pondered how many were employed

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
used means were employed

explanation.surface: Wondering how big the workforce was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Mused means thought deeply or reflected.

clue.text: One of an opening pair

parts.note: suggests a cricket opening batsman, but describes what a door swings on, usually fitted in twos

explanation.surface: One of the two opening batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A door usually swings on two of these jointed fittings.

clue.text: Sounds like more work for the tenants

indicators.note: Sounds like says the word wanted is said the same as a phrase

parts.note: more work means less ease

explanation.surface: Extra chores for the people renting the house.
explanation.walkthrough: LESS EASE said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessees hold a property on a lease, as renters do.

clue.text: Flowers one sees periodically

explanation.surface: Blooms that appear every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is publications such as yearbooks, issued once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: These plants complete their life cycle within a year; the word also means yearly books or periodicals.

clue.text: Told next of kin

explanation.surface: Informed the family of a death.
explanation.definitionFit: Related means recounted, as a story is; it also means connected by family ties.

clue.text: Magnetic holders?

parts.note: suggests things held on by magnets, but describes iron bars laid across a magnet's poles to keep its strength

explanation.surface: Fridge magnets holding notes in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft-iron bar placed across a horseshoe magnet's poles preserves its magnetism and goes by this name.
